title: Per-request attribution flow & sketch notes for token cost + latency explorer
body:
Purpose
-----
This is a working sketch doc for a per-request attribution flow inside the Console explorer that surfaces token-level cost and latency contributions for a single request or aggregated cohort. Goal: give engineers and product owners a quick way to diagnose why an endpoint saw a sudden cost or latency regression and which parts of the request or model stack contributed the most.

Context and problem statement
-----------------------------
- Product team needs a panel that can: correlate per-request tokens with downstream cost (quantization, batch size, kernel choice), show where latency was spent (encode, decode, kv-lookup, queuing), and allow one-click rollbacks to previous runtime configs or model variants.
- Current Console dashboards show aggregate SLOs and per-model metrics but not request-level attribution, making postmortems slow.
- This doc tracks low-fidelity UX ideas, acceptance criteria, and backlog items for grooming.

Primary user personas
---------------------
1) Platform engineer on-call: wants to triage a spike quickly and revert a rollout or adjust batching.
2) ML infra owner: wants to correlate slowdown to quantization or a new kernel rollout.
3) App engineer/product manager: wants to see if user prompts changed token mix and cost.

Key user stories
----------------
- As an on-call engineer, I can open a single-request view from errors table and see a timeline of where the tokens were consumed and how that maps to cost, so I can identify whether a model change or traffic pattern caused the regression.
- As a product owner, I can select a cohort (last hour, user segment) and surface the top 5 tokens or prompt templates driving cost increases.
- As an infra engineer, I can see whether KV cache hits prevented recomputation and how caching changed before/after a rollout.

High-level UI components proposed
--------------------------------
1) Request header bar (top)
   - Request id, timestamp, route, model, variant, region, commit id
   - Quick actions: open logs, rollback variant, re-run request
2) Waterfall timeline (center-left)
   - Horizontal timeline with stacked swimlanes: queuing, encode, attention kernels, kv-lookup, decode, network wait
   - Hover shows ms and token counts per segment
3) Token-attribution sparkline (center-right)
   - Compact waterfall per-token type (prompt, system, user, assistant) with cost-per-token overlay (currency/tokens)
   - Toggle between absolute and normalized views
4) Cost breakdown card (right column)
   - Itemized rows: model compute, batch overhead, cache delta, network egress, quantization penalty
   - Each row is clickable to open config diffs and corresponding change history
5) Compare mode (bottom)
   - Side-by-side request comparison or baseline vs current variant with color-coded diffs
6) Quick filters and query bar (top-left)
   - Filter by status code, latency bucket, token range, user segment, model variant

Wireframe notes (low fidelity sketches)
--------------------------------------
- Sketch A: Single-column focus view. Timeline left, token bar right, cost slice bottom. Clean for mobile but lacks quick compare.
- Sketch B: Two-column engineer view. Timeline + token attribution on left, action cards + logs on right. Good for triage.
- Sketch C: Cohort explorer. Compact table of requests with inline sparklines and a detail pane. Useful for sampling large traffic.

Interaction patterns and affordances
----------------------------------
- Hover reveals absolute ms and token counts; click pins a segment to open 'where-to-fix' modal.
- Clicking a cost row opens a diff widget comparing runtime config X vs Y (shows batching, quantization flags, kernel set).
- Deep link support: each request view has a stable URL to share in PagerDuty/Slack.
- Play button to 'replay' timeline at variable speed for educational demos.

Metrics to surface and acceptance criteria
----------------------------------------
- Must show end-to-end latency and per-segment latency with +/- 5% accuracy compared to SRE traces.
- Cost estimate should match billing within 2% for token compute and 5% for additional overheads (network, egress).
- UI must allow triage action (rollback or pin variant) within 2 clicks from request row.

Grooming/backlog items (rough priorities + story points)
-------------------------------------------------------
- INF-2147: Backend: request attribution query API (priority: P0, 8 pts)
- INF-2148: UI: Waterfall timeline component (P0, 5 pts)
- INF-2149: UI: Token-attribution sparkline and cost overlay (P1, 3 pts)
- INF-2150: Integrations: link to Rollouts service and config diffs (P1, 5 pts)
- INF-2151: Cohort sampler + CSV export (P2, 3 pts)
- INF-2152: E2E tests for accuracy vs billing and traces (P0, 8 pts)
- INF-2160: Mobile responsive tweaks (P3, 2 pts)

Open questions / unresolved design tradeoffs
------------------------------------------
- Level of precision vs performance: full per-token attribution is expensive to compute for high-volume endpoints. Do we sample requests by default? Proposal: sample old requests for cohort view, full resolution for explicit single-request inspection.
- Currency display: show cost in account default currency or normalized units (token-units). UX needs to avoid surprising finance teams.
- Privacy: do we mask prompt contents by default? Recommend redaction toggle for PII-sensitive routes.

Notes to self / meeting fragments
--------------------------------
- Miguel suggested adding a "hot-spot" compact view that surfaces the top 3 tokens with highest compute multiplier.
- Lina: follow-up with SLA team to align on how we surface infra fallback events (region fallback, fallback model).
- Samir: confirm data retention window for request-level traces (likely 30 days by default).

Next steps and meeting agenda for 2024-03-07 sync
------------------------------------------------
1) Decide sampling defaults for cohort vs single-request (Aisha + Infra)
2) Align on cost calculation config and currency handling (FinOps + Product)
3) Sign off on waterfall swimlane names and hover payload (UX + SRE)
4) Kick off INF-2147 with API contract stub and example payloads (backend)
notes: working doc, rough sketches and action items; not polished; for team discussion
